摘要

橫空出世的恐怖傳奇：《P.T.》的震撼登場

作者回顧，2014 年 8 月的 Gamescom 展會上，一款掛名虛擬工作室「7780s」的神秘作品《P.T.》無預警免費登陸 PlayStation Store。遊戲透過狹窄且無限循環的居家走廊、毛骨悚然的嬰兒哭聲以及隨時尾隨在後的幽靈麗莎（Lisa），營造出極致壓抑的恐怖氛圍，迅速在全球掀起現象級狂潮。當玩家解開重重謎題逃離迴廊後，才震撼發現這部「可遊玩預告片」（Playable Teaser）實為小島秀夫主導的《沉默之丘》（Silent Hills）全新續作，更網羅了奧斯卡名導吉勒摩·戴托羅、知名影星諾曼·瑞杜斯以及恐怖漫畫大師伊藤潤二攜手合作，讓全球玩家的期待值攀升至頂點。

驟然殞落與徹底抹除：小島秀夫與 Konami 的決裂

然而就在玩家翹首盼望正式作品時，小島秀夫與 Konami 高層的關係卻在《潛龍諜影V：幻痛》開發期間急遽惡化，小島團隊不僅面臨內部網路切斷與宣傳除名，小島本人也被降格為約聘狀態。2015 年 4 月，吉勒摩·戴托羅公開證實《沉默之丘》開發計畫遭到取消，Konami 不僅中止專案，更直接將《P.T.》從 PlayStation Store 徹底下架並禁止重新下載。這項前所未有的舉動引發玩家憤怒，亦導致已安裝該遊戲的 PS4 二手主機價格暴漲至數千美元的天價；外界甚至盛傳下架原因與遊戲通關後暗諷管理層的台詞激怒官方有關。

深遠影響與不死精神：後續波瀾與恐怖遊戲新標竿

《P.T.》的消失促使許多獨立團隊試圖打造精神續作，亦有一名 17 歲粉絲自行重製 PC 版，雖因版權遭 Konami 叫停，卻意外獲得周邊補償與實習機會。在 2015 年的 The Game Awards（TGA）頒獎典禮上，小島秀夫甚至受到 Konami 律師函警告而無法親自領獎，引發全球玩家與業界好友的強烈不滿。作者總結，小島秀夫在離開後帶領核心團隊成立全新的 Kojima Productions 浴火重生，而短暫存在的《P.T.》雖然命運多舛，卻以其革命性的恐怖手法深刻啟發了後世無數作品，成為電玩歷史上無可替代的傳奇符號。

================================================

If you ask players what the scariest horror game they've ever played is, I believe everyone would have a different answer. It might be the jump-scaring toys in Five Nights at Freddy's, the adaptive AI in Alien: Isolation, or perhaps the Outlast series that's known for needing diapers. But when it comes to the scariest playable teaser, we have to mention this title that sends chills down people's spines with just two letters. Hi, hello everyone, welcome to Player's Journey. Years ago, the concept. horror game P.T., co-created by Hideo Kojima, terrified countless players. Even I, a veteran of so many horror games, was left completely humbled, which successfully sparked everyone's anticipation for the full release. However, before players could wait for the full game to launch, the entire project was cancelled, and P.T. itself was even pulled from the PlayStation Store, making consoles that still had the game installed incredibly precious. Recently, with the development of reverse engineering technology, someone has successfully ported this long-discontinued game to PC, making. many fans feel as if they've seen its resurrection. And even Hideo Kojima himself seems to have expressed his support for this. Why exactly did this globally viral work face such a tragic fate, and what kind of charm does it have that players still can't forget it after over a decade? Next, Player's Journey will share the story behind P.T. with you all. If there’s anything missed or if you'd like to add anything, feel free to leave a comment below. And before the video starts, remember to like and subscribe to our channel, and don't forget to hit the notification bell so you don't miss our updates! Back in August 2014, at the Gamescom Sony. press conference, a trailer for something called P.T. suddenly appeared . The screen showed only a pseudonym " 7780s," a mundane suburban hallway, a bag full of cockroaches, and finally, the reaction of players screaming in terror at the time. Subsequently, this game was released for free on the PlayStation Store, attracting a huge number of players to download and experience it, wanting to see if it was really as scary as they said. After opening the game, the narrow hallway, the endlessly looping space, the disturbing baby cries, and Lisa, who always follows behind the player, all made players feel the immense oppressive.

atmosphere created by this work. Every time I opened a door, I clearly saw the same scene, yet creepy changes would always occur. Especially when I saw her standing in front of me, a player who loves yet fears horror like me chose to stand still rather than move forward or shut the game down. In the end, almost everyone who played it was scared senseless and afraid to continue, while those without a PS4 console flocked to YouTube to watch gameplay videos or streams. Whatwant. >> I think you should take this chance, before he mentions it, to stop watching ahead. Within less than a day of its release, P.T. caused a sensation in the gaming world, and the player community began to wonder what secrets were hidden behind this game. Enthusiastic players scrambled to unearth every clue in the game, eventually solving the puzzles and finding a way to escape the endless corridor. But I’m different; I beat the game by following the methods others had found. Upon successfully escaping the corridor, the game plays a cinematic, and only then do players realize this isn't some brand new IP, but the Silent. Hill series installment, Silent Hills, co-produced by Hideo Kojima. It’s perfectly normal that players didn't know at first; after all, P.T. takes place entirely indoors, and since you can't see the iconic fog of the Silent Hill series, it naturally doesn't feel like a part of the franchise. The " 7780s" that appears at the start of the game actually hides an Easter egg: 7780 refers to the area of the town of Totsukawa in square kilometers, and when broken down and translated, it hints at Silent Hill. P.T. itself is just an abbreviation for "Playable Teaser," meaning it was simply an interactive trailer used by Hideo Kojima to reveal the new Silent Hill title. Furthermore,. Norman Reedus, the actor who later starred as the protagonist in Death Stranding, was already slated to provide his likeness for Silent Hills long before. Renowned Mexican film director Guillermo del Toro was also set to participate in the production. It was later confirmed that famed horror manga artist Junji Ito had also been invited to work on the project. Interestingly, Hideo Kojima revealed in a past interview that when the president of Konami invited him to make the next Silent Hill, he admitted that he gets scared easily by horror movies and wasn't confident he could handle it, but he also felt that because he was so easily frightened, he might be able to.

create a unique horror experience. Additionally, he was happy to participate if he could supervise or provide the Fox Engine technology to help the series continue. At a talk event, Hideo Kojima even mentioned that he and Guillermo del Toro originally only hoped to scare the pants off players, but they changed their minds and decided they wanted to scare them to death, joking that the limited edition of the game might even come with a spare pair of pants. A month later at the Tokyo Game Show, Kojima Productions unveiled a brand new concept trailer, showcasing even more disturbing imagery . From a rolling ball turning into a human head, to centipedes crawling out. of walls, and a headless giant chasing players, these eerie scenes maxed out player expectations, making me feel "I need that more than anything right now. " I want it. >> Just as players were eagerly awaiting the official release of Silent Hills, events took a turn that nobody wanted. Less than a year after P.T. launched, the relationship between Hideo Kojima and Konami had completely deteriorated. In truth, tensions had been building since the development of Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain. As internal restructuring began, Kojima Productions. faced various restrictions; staff were even cut off from company internet, email, and phone access. Hideo Kojima’s own status within the company shifted from a permanent employee to something akin to a contractor. Meanwhile, Kojima’s name gradually vanished from promotional materials, and even the studio’s logo was removed. However, some players still refused to believe it, until April 2015 when Guillermo del Toro confirmed at an event that the collaboration on Silent Hills would not be moving forward, leaving him... ...and Norman Reedus expressed their own regrets on Twitter. As the news spread, it was officially confirmed that Silent Hills would no longer be in development . But it wasn't just the cancellation; Konami actually pulled P.T. from the PlayStation Store. Even worse, players who had already added it to their libraries couldn't redownload it; once you deleted it or switched consoles, it was gone forever. Consequently, people began auctioning off PS4 consoles with P.T. installed on the secondhand market , with prices skyrocketing to thousands of dollars—a reminder that while the.

game was free when it was playable, it cost a fortune when it wasn't. As for why Konami pulled P.T., officials only stated that the game’s licensing period on the PlayStation Store was ending. However, players pointed to a line of dialogue after beating P.T. that sounded as if Hideo Kojima was secretly... Ko-. -nami. Thus, some players speculated that this line, mirroring reality, infuriated Konami, leading them to decide to take P.T. down. The disappearance of P.T. also led many developers to attempt to create works with similar styles, hoping. to recreate that suffocating horror experience. Titles like Allison Road and The Peterson Case drew attention for their resemblance to P.T., yet none of them were ever officially released. During this time, a 17-year-old fan personally created a remake called P.T. for PC, but the project was ultimately shut down by Konami due to legal issues , forcing him to stop development and take it offline. However, this fan also mentioned that a Konami representative told him that many people within the company actually liked his work. In addition to sending him some game merchandise, they even offered him an internship at Konami, which was a very. special experience for him while he was still in high school. As for other players, upon learning their anticipated game was canceled, they vented their anger directly at Konami. The iconic slogan of that time could be seen everywhere on Twitter, forums, and video titles. Even Guillermo del Toro later replied "F***Konami" when Hideo Kojima commemorated the eighth anniversary of P.T., showing their dissatisfaction was no less than the players '. But no matter how much the players protested, there was no turning back; Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain ultimately became Hideo Kojima's final work at Konami. Ironically, not only did this.

game receive acclaim from many players, but it also won the Best Action/ Adventure game award at TGA 2015. However, it wasn't Kojima himself who went on stage to accept the award, but the voice actor for Venom Snake. At the time, TGA host Geoff Keighley explained directly to the audience that Hideo Kojima had received a notice from Konami's lawyers before the ceremony, stating that he was not allowed to attend that night. award >> After leaving, Kojima did not stop there . Just as the lines in P.T. suggested, he formed Kojima Productions with his core team and returned to players with brand-new works. Meanwhile, Konami continued to focus on other business ventures, leaving the Silent Hill series dormant for a long time until recent years, when they finally announced remakes and new projects to bring it back into the public eye. Although it was tragically pulled from stores, the. impact it had on the entire gaming industry was significant. It forced many developers to rethink the storytelling methods and immersion of first-person psychological horror games, using cramped spaces and subtle, unsettling environmental changes to build psychological terror that doesn't just rely on jumpscares. Therefore, apart from fan-made remakes, there are actually many horror games on the market inspired by P.T. For example, the developers of Layers of Fear explicitly stated that P.T. showed them the market demand for psychological horror; instead of just having monsters chase players, they preferred to create fear through. the environment, atmosphere, and constantly shifting scenes. The once-viral "Exit 8" is a horror game that traps players in a constantly looping underground passage, forcing them to carefully observe their surroundings and turn back the moment they spot anything unusual. Although its gameplay isn't exactly the same as P.T. , the developer mentioned that P.T. was indeed one of the inspirations for the game. In addition, the development team behind Resident Evil Village didn't explicitly state that P.T. was an inspiration, but in the Beneviento House level, players are not only stripped of their weapons but also forced to explore.

dim corridors and even encounter a giant baby that gave many players nightmares. This design, which deliberately deprives players of security and uses the environment and psychological pressure to create fear, reminded many players and industry insiders of P.T. What the freak? P.T. >> Hideo Kojima surely never imagined that the name of a game he helped develop would become an adjective; another adjective I know is "Discord." Interestingly, the influence of this work even extended to the world of adult. games. For example, an adult game called "Chain Wolf" tasks players with avoiding a massive monster in a looping space, where being caught leads to big trouble . Plus, just looking at the opening scene of the game, players know exactly which game it was inspired by without needing to be told. Even though I'm trembling, as a gentleman, I'm still a bit excited. Is this what they call "if you're brave enough, even a ghost can ..."? Comeback. Before we knew it, it's already 2026, and what neither the gaming community nor Hideo Kojima expected was that he would face a situation similar to the one he had back at Konami. This time,. Sony announced its withdrawal from developing the action-espionage game " Physint" with Kojima Productions, once leaving the project on the verge of being canceled. Regarding this incident , I have already made a video sharing it , so interested players can go check it out. Fortunately, this project was luckier. After Sony pulled out, Kojima Productions actively sought new partners , and ultimately, Xbox took over publishing, allowing "Physint" to continue development. Long before that, Hideo Kojima had actually been working with Xbox to develop another horror game , also consisting of two letters: "OD." Seeing Hideo Kojima return to the horror. genre, many fans are naturally excited and expectant, hoping to see a P.T.- level horror experience in this game. However, with the precedent from back then, many players are starting to get PTSD, worrying that Xbox might pull something similar in the future, with many joking that "OD" actually stands for "Only Demo"— "Remember to download the demo, and whatever you do, don't delete it.""I guess we can only blame Hideo Kojima for being bad at naming horror games; he should have called it FR, then players would believe the game could FRelease." To the surprise of many , a developer named LavenZavier recently succeeded in porting the long-discontinued P.T. to PC. Unlike.

other fan-made remakes, this one uses reverse engineering to rebuild the game's engine and rendering system, restoring the original scenes, sound effects, and puzzle flow as accurately as possible. Regarding the stir that reverse engineering has caused in the gaming world, the creator "Jimi" has made a video about it in the past; interested players can go check it out. The news quickly gained support from many players, and even renowned game data miner Lance McDonald gave high praise to the fidelity of this port. What was even more unexpected for LavenZavier was that Kojima himself noticed the project and retweeted a. report introducing this port, leaving LavenZavier incredibly thrilled. However , as the project received more attention , LavenZavier also began to face attacks from some players, with some even accusing him of faking it and sending him terrifying threats. Facing this malicious feedback, he stated that he would significantly reduce the time spent on the project; while he might release fixes and updates in the future , he no longer promises continuous active development. This led some players to speculate that LavenZavier's porting project might have impacted the collector's value of PS4 consoles that still have P.T. installed, which is why some people attacked him. Although many. players are unhappy with those attacking the developer, others believe that the fact LavenZavier enabled more players to experience P.T. on PC is already very meaningful. P.T. was originally just a free demo intended to tease Silent Hills , but unexpectedly, with its unique horror experience, it not only became a classic in horror game history but also influenced the design of many later games. Even though Hideo Kojima and Konami have parted ways, players still haven't forgotten this work, and developers are even striving to let more people experience the original P.T. on PC. One can only hope the upcoming OD makes it to an official release and. isn't just a "lyDemo." I wonder what you , the players, think about the story behind P.T.? 面對社群日益擴大的反彈聲浪，VRChat 官方隨後公開回應，承認 AI 帶來粗製濫造內容的隱憂，但也認為 AI 在代碼輔助與多語言翻譯上具有正面效益。為了制定合適政策，官方發起了一份為期七天的問卷調查，迅速收集到超過兩萬份回饋與深度訪談。調查中最引人注目的結果顯示，有高達 95% 的玩家明確支持平台應為 AI 生成內容增設標籤與分類過濾功能，讓社群原以為這項訴求已成定局。

================================================

If you learned that 95%of your players wanted the platform to label AI-generated content, would you meet their demands? Hello, everyone, and welcome to Player Files. Facing increasing community pressure, VRChat......quickly responded publicly to the matter. However, they also believe AI.

is not without its benefits; after all, some creators use AI to assist with coding and translating different languages, allowing their work to be better and reach players in more regions . So, it mainly comes down to how those people use AI. Therefore, VRChat does not want to dismiss all creators who use AI just because some AI-generated content is of poor quality. To address this, they proposed several directions, including updating creator guidelines to prohibit the use of world thumbnails that mislead players. In other words, regardless of whether an image is AI-generated, if a player enters a world and finds the content doesn't match the promotional image, it may violate. platform guidelines. Actually, you don't even need to go in to find the difference; the various AI-generated food images and posters in real life are already enough for a nerd like me to tell whether something is an AI image. >> My AI radar is very sharp. The official team also plans to improve the discovery and recommendation systems for worlds and avatars, giving well-crafted works more exposure while allowing players to provide feedback directly in-game, so creators know how their work is being received. As for the most discussed topic—AI and AI content filtering—the officials couldn't make a decision. They feel it's not impossible, but they don't. know how to distinguish between different levels of AI usage or under what circumstances creators should be required to disclose their use of AI. So , they decided to continue communicating with the community and created a survey , giving players seven days to provide their suggestions. In just seven short days, this survey received over 20,000 responses. To better understand how different players view AI, the officials also conducted one-on-one interviews with some creators. The most striking figure from the entire survey was that a staggering 95%of players want the platform to add AI tags. Just when the player community thought this was a sure. win, the officials had more to say. Although a huge number of players want AI tags, the officials believe other survey results show this doesn't represent......that players completely reject AI. They then started pulling out a mountain of data to prove that players are actually still accepting of AI-assisted creation. For instance, when asked how to label works for eight different AI usage scenarios, players proposed over 3,000 different tag combinations, with none receiving more than 10%support. Therefore, the officials argue that while most players want more.

transparency regarding AI use, there is no consensus on when to tag or how to categorize them. Wait, how did the player community become the ones responsible for solving this problem? Furthermore, they pointed out that only 33%of players said they would deliberately avoid AI-assisted content, and among those who left written feedback, only 37%expressed similar views. Regardless of all that, it doesn't change the fact that 95%of players want AI tags, so many players expected the. officials to meet the majority's needs. To everyone's surprise, VRChat ultimately decided not to launch AI tags or provide AI content filtering. Wish I could, but I can't. Well, I could , but I won't, maybe, but in short—no. >> This decision left many players feeling completely stunned. Having put effort into filling out the survey, it backfired, only making the officials more confused about why tags are even needed. Content creators have pointed out that players have clearly expressed their desire for the platform to add AI labels. As for how these labels should be designed, they could easily release. an initial version and adjust it based on player feedback, rather than doing nothing at all just because they can't find a solution that satisfies everyone . Many players have sarcastically quipped, "95%of survey respondents want AI usage to be labeled in some way, but that’s not what our investors want to see, so you’ll just have to keep consuming this junk content—and you’ll like it, too. What a shame.""95%of people in the desert want water, but some want it in a cup, some want it bottled, some want a tap, and others want it in a kettle. Ultimately, we conclude that the desert residents want to die of thirst, because they couldn't. reach a consensus on how to get water, so we won't give it to them." However, there are other reasons why officials are refusing to introduce AI labels. Since labels rely on creator self-reporting, they worry that some might be dishonest, and they also fear that AI labels could trigger new forms of community harassment, with some players acting like detectives to hunt down works suspected of using AI and harassing the creators. Why does this sound so familiar? The person who said this seems to have been mocked by quite a few players. Nevertheless, many players believe these reasons are simply not enough to serve as an excuse for.

refusing to increase transparency. After all, what players have been asking for from the start isn't a ban on AI works on the platform, but for the platform to provide them with a choice. Content creators have pointed out that consumers need to know if a product uses AI so that everyone can make choices based on their own values; in this regard, Steam is still far ahead. Some don't mind AI, while others don't want to engage with AI-generated content ; that is a consumer's freedom. Therefore, he believes that using potential harassment as an excuse to deny a consumer-friendly transparency feature is just an attempt to shirk responsibility. He even criticized this behavior not as cowardice, but as a deliberate attempt to use any excuse possible to avoid doing the right thing. >> As for the AI content filtering feature , officials argue that once players set up filter criteria, they might miss out. on that content forever. This explanation was similarly blasted by players, who stated that they are setting the filters precisely because they don't want to see that content. Although the officials refused to implement an AI tag, they lean toward using a "Human-Made" label, allowing creators who don't use AI to identify their work as human-made. At the same time, to better understand the boundaries of AI labeling, they are conducting a single-question survey, asking players to help them answer it. Wait, didn't you just say that you refused to launch an AI tag because you were worried creators would hide their AI usage? Following that logic, if I use. AI to create, can't I also just mark my own work as human-made? Consequently, this method, which also appears to have loopholes, naturally makes many players feel that it cannot effectively solve the problem of information transparency . Because they didn't listen to the 95% of players, and even their provided explanation failed to convince the community, VRChat quickly drew heavy criticism. Players felt the officials didn't respect their opinions at all, and the selective ignoring of the statistics they provided left players questioning the point of asking for community input in the first place. Some sarcastically mocked VRChat for protecting low-quality AI-generated.

content, even quipping, "I didn't know TamSwiny was on your board of directors . We wanted you to fill out the survey, not answer it like this." Furthermore, to express their dissatisfaction, some players even unsubscribed from VRChat Plus and called on others to vote with their wallets. On the day the officials announced the survey results and their final decision , those 95%of players quickly went to Steam to leave negative reviews. Currently, the positive rating in the English-speaking region has already fallen to 30%. Even the Halloween event. VRChat originally planned to host was affected, with two DJs publicly announcing their withdrawal from the event due to dissatisfaction with the official decision. Interestingly, since the officials refused to use an AI tag, the players decided to do it themselves . Because Steam's community tagging system isn't just for game developers— as long as players have a qualified, unrestricted account, they can add tags to games themselves. Steam then sorts them by tag weight, and only the top 20 tags are displayed on the store page, so dissatisfied players started mass-tagging it as AI. As a result, on. November 1st, an "Artificial Intelligence" tag actually appeared on VRChat's Steam store page for a time, and Steam won without doing anything because they had long provided a feature for players to tag games themselves. However, the tag only lasted for about a day before disappearing, and the reason remains unclear. Although VRChat's refusal to add AI tags might be due to concerns about predatory behavior, it’s quite abstract to ignore a survey where 95%of users want the feature. One can only hope the game finds a solution that satisfies player needs without compromising the experience. What are your thoughts on the recent controversies surrounding VRChat? wild. Indeed, many players initially felt the combat feedback was a bit off and found the visuals in the prologue rough. either. 畫面變清晰，遊戲卻更不穩定

完全版上市後，玩家發現它雖然提升了部分畫面清晰度，整體表現卻遠低於期待。作者提到，簡體中文版 Steam 好評率只有約 10%，英文版也僅約 17%。玩家在世界地圖與戰鬥中遭遇掉幀、卡頓和閃退，舊有問題沒有修好，還出現新錯誤。原本期待新版本能在現代電腦上運作得更順暢，結果反而得在 4K 畫面下忍受低 FPS。

took the same images and asked an AI to upscale them with a single prompt, and the results turned out better than what the developers produced. it belonged to a high-level executive at CA. He also admitted that the team was focused on other major projects at the time and failed to adequately oversee the external development work. Although no name was. mentioned directly, players widely believe that a Polish studio called Mardum was responsible for its development and that the project was categorized as a full-cycle remaster. This remaster was also outsourced to another company, and it crashed upon launch, with players criticizing it for numerous bugs, unstable performance, and the alteration or removal of much classic content. What angered players even more was that before the Definitive Edition was released, the original trilogy was pulled from multiple platforms, forcing.

users to choose the Definitive Edition for a period of time. As for why they didn't just port it directly instead of using a remaster? How else would they squeeze a bit more money out of the players? Of course, before Shogun 2 Collection, Sega actually released another title that sparked similar controversy: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine-Mastercrafted Edition, developed with Relic Entertainment and published by Sega. It also cost $ 40 and aimed to bring improvements to graphics, controls , and the interface of the 2011 original . However, after its release, players felt it didn't meet the standards of a true remaster, leading to criticism upon. launch. Its Steam rating once dropped to about 30%positive, and its peak concurrent player count was even lower than Shogun 2 Collection, at just 128 people. The only difference is that Sega did not delist the original version at the time, so players didn't have to spend extra money to buy the new version . This situation has led some content creators to question whether Sega has adopted a more cautious strategy toward its Western gaming business in recent years. After all, they have indeed sold off or divested some related assets in the past, so they speculate that Sega may be looking to improve the financial performance of its Western operations. while lowering development costs and upfront risks. In contrast, the remasters or re-releases of Sega's Persona series in recent years have maintained higher production standards, and the titles in the Like a Dragon series are still led by their original development teams. Overall, the reason the Shogun 2 Complete Edition sparked such widespread player dissatisfaction is not only due to the game being riddled with bugs and poor performance, but also the discovery that it used low-quality AI-generated assets. Added to this is the severing of the modding community that the original game had built up over many years, which led players to feel that the Complete Edition was inferior to the original. Now, due to overwhelming negative.

reviews, the Complete Edition has been temporarily pulled by the publisher, and the original version has returned. One can only hope that when game companies decide to remaster beloved classic titles, they will genuinely focus on improving game quality, rather than just releasing a new version that exploits player nostalgia, turning a classic that should be cherished into a commercial tool that erodes trust. 值得閱讀的理由

  • 探討電玩界關於「虛構受害者角色能否商品化」的敏感道德邊界，以及社群雙重標準的諷刺論戰。
  • 一窺飾演該角色的演員本人如何用最真實的熱愛，化解並反擊網路上的過度解讀。

摘要

萬聖節驚喜聯動與病嬌女友熱潮

每年萬聖節，《Fortnite 要塞英雄》都會推出豐富的節慶活動。在 2026 年的活動中，官方除了帶來經典恐怖 IP 與人氣作品外，最引人注目的莫過於聯動了以超低成本締造數億美元票房奇蹟的恐怖電影《愛你，至死不渝》。劇中由演員 Indey Salvestrini 飾演的病嬌女主角 Nikki，憑藉令人背脊發涼的神情反差風靡全球，其標誌性的服裝與經典台詞動作也在遊戲中高度還原，引起極大話題。

推特玩家抗議：消費受害者與道德爭議

然而造型公開後，卻在社群平台 Twitter（X） 上引發部分網友強烈不滿。抗議者指出，Nikki 在電影中是被超自然惡意實體奪走意識並遭受身體控制，本質上是一名遭受心靈虐待與侵犯的「受害者」。反對者認為 Epic Games 將這樣的悲劇角色做成可操控、奔跑跳舞的造型，是在將嚴肅的創傷議題娛樂化，甚至有人憤而呼籲全面抵制遊戲。

荒謬的雙標質疑與虛實難分的論戰

面對抵制聲浪，廣大玩家社群紛紛出面反擊，認為這場爭議荒謬至極。作者與許多玩家指出，遊戲過去早已聯動過無數在原作中身為受害者或極端加害者的角色，卻從未遭遇如此嚴厲的道德審判。眾多玩家嘲諷反對者分不清「虛構與現實」，對虛擬角色的過度同情甚至超過了現實中的苦難，使得這場爭論逐漸演變成網路群體間的文化筆戰。

演員親自破除爭議，以熱愛回擊質疑

儘管網路吵得沸沸揚揚，Nikki 的飾演者 Indey 本人本身就是重度遊戲玩家與實況主。她不僅欣然授權形象，更在社群媒體上熱情分享自己使用 Nikki 造型遊玩《Fortnite》的畫面，對這次聯動展現出由衷的喜愛與支持。演員本人的大方力挺，直接讓抗議者的「代為抱不平」顯得格外諷刺，也讓這場抵制風波在玩家的嘲諷與笑聲中逐漸平息。
